313	/**
314	 * How far one claim moved, as the engine read it.
315	 *
316	 * Every part of it is the engine's own: the two readings, the sign that says
317	 * which way it went, the share of versions that agreed, and whether the move
318	 * came from nothing but the observation changing how much each version counts.
319	 * Nothing here subtracts, compares two numbers, or works anything out.
320	 *
321	 * @param row The claim's own row of the engine's difference.
322	 */
323	function movement(row: ClaimDiff): Movement | undefined {
324	  const { before, after, delta, agreement } = row;
325	  if (before === null || after === null || delta === null) {
326	    return undefined;
327	  }
328	  return {
329	    from: before,
330	    to: after,
331	    // Which way it went is the sign of the engine's own difference. Reading a
332	    // sign is a comparison against nought, not a subtraction: nothing here works
333	    // out how far anything moved.
334	    way: delta < 0 ? "down" : "up",
335	    by: delta,
336	    sameDirection:
337	      agreement === null
338	        ? {
339	            absence: noReadingAtAll(
340	              "Only one of the two worlds holds this claim, so there is no direction for the " +
341	                "versions of the map to have agreed or disagreed about.",
342	            ),
343	          }
344	        : { reading: agreement },
345	    // A claim with no causes of its own can move under **This happened** without
346	    // anything pushing on it: the observation makes the versions of the map in
347	    // which it was likely count for more, and the average shifts. The engine
348	    // says when that is the whole story, and the panel prints one sentence when
349	    // it does. **The browser never works this out for itself** — it is a fact
350	    // about how the engine read the numbers, and only the engine knows it.
351	    onlyReweighted: row.moved_only_by_reweighting,
352	  };
353	}
354	
355	/** Turn the engine's difference into what the rail and the tiles read. */
356	function toDiffView(difference: Diff, claims: readonly ClaimView[]): DiffView {
357	  const byId = new Map(claims.map((claim) => [claim.id, claim]));
358	
359	  const changed = new Map<string, ClaimChange>();
360	  for (const [id, one] of Object.entries(difference.claims)) {
361	    changed.set(id, {
362	      state: one.state,
363	      moved: movement(one),
364	    });
365	  }
366	
367	  // The endings that moved, in the engine's own order, largest rank first.
368	  // Nothing here sorts, re-ranks or drops a row.
369	  const ranked: DeltaRow[] = difference.rows.map((row): DeltaRow => {
370	    const claim = byId.get(row.target);
371	    return {
372	      claimId: row.target,
373	      label: claim?.claim ?? NOT_ON_THIS_MAP,
374	      kind: claim?.kind ?? "market",
375	      move: {
376	        reading: {
377	          from: row.before,
378	          to: row.after,
379	          largestOn: row.at_day,
380	          way: row.peak_delta < 0 ? "down" : "up",
381	          by: row.peak_delta,
382	        },
383	      },
384	      rangeWidth: { reading: row.range_width },
385	      agreement: { reading: row.agreement },
386	    };
387	  });
388	
389	  // An ending the engine left off that list did not move. Silence cannot be
390	  // told from absence — a reader would not know whether the ending held still
391	  // or is simply not on this map — so it gets a quiet row of its own, after
392	  // every ranked row and never mixed in among them.
393	  const listed = new Set(ranked.map((row) => row.claimId));
394	  const held: DeltaRow[] = claims
395	    .filter(
396	      (claim) =>
397	        (claim.kind === "market" || claim.kind === "not_tradeable") &&
398	        !listed.has(claim.id) &&
399	        changed.get(claim.id)?.state === "unchanged",
400	    )
401	    .map((claim) => ({
402	      claimId: claim.id,
403	      label: claim.claim,
404	      kind: claim.kind,
405	      move: {
406	        absence: inTheEnginesWords(
407	          NO_CHANGE,
408	          `${noChangeReason(changed.get(claim.id)?.moved)} It is listed so that holding still ` +
409	            `cannot be mistaken for not being here.`,
410	        ),
411	      },
412	      rangeWidth: {
413	        absence: noReadingAtAll(
414	          "How firm a number is only says something about a number that moved.",
415	        ),
416	      },
417	      agreement: {
418	        absence: noReadingAtAll(
419	          "Whether the versions of the map agreed on a direction only says something about a " +
420	            "claim that had a direction.",
421	        ),
422	      },
423	      noChange: true,
424	    }));
425	
426	  const summary: Known<string> = { reading: difference.summary };
427	  return { claims: changed, rows: [...ranked, ...held], summary, warnings: difference.warnings };
428	}

430	/**
431	 * The branch in the shape that goes over the wire, or a sentence saying why it
432	 * cannot go.
433	 *
434	 * A branch is only askable about when every edit in it can be written down the
435	 * way the server writes one. Today one edit cannot: a claim of your own needs
436	 * the part of this product that drafts a whole claim — its wording, how it is
437	 * judged, by whom, by when — and that is not connected.
438	 *
439	 * @param branch The branch the screen is showing.
440	 * @throws Error With one plain sentence, when the branch cannot be sent.
441	 */
442	function sendable(branch: BranchView): WireBranch {
443	  if (branch.wire === undefined) {
444	    throw new Error(
445	      `The branch "${branch.label}" has an edit this build cannot hand to the engine, so no ` +
446	        `world was asked for. Adding a claim of your own needs the part of this product that ` +
447	        `drafts one, and that is not connected yet.`,
448	    );
449	  }
450	  return branch.wire;
451	}

453	/**
454	 * Calls the engine for a computed world, for what an edit moved, and for the
455	 * number on one arrow.
456	 *
457	 * It keeps one thing between calls: the stored example itself, because a map is
458	 * written by hand and does not change while the page is open. It keeps no
459	 * world, no difference and no likelihood — those are computed results, and a
460	 * kept one eventually disagrees with the three things it came from.
461	 */
462	export class ApiWorldSource implements WorldSource {
463	  /** The stored examples this page has already read, by their short names. */
464	  readonly #maps = new Map<string, Promise<FixtureBundle>>();
465	
466	  /** The base map and its branches, read once and kept for as long as the page is open. */
467	  async readBundle(id: string): Promise<FixtureBundle> {
468	    const already = this.#maps.get(id);
469	    if (already !== undefined) {
470	      return already;
471	    }
472	    const asked = readExample(id);
473	    this.#maps.set(id, asked);
474	    try {
475	      return await asked;
476	    } catch (failure) {
477	      // A map that could not be read is not a map we should go on pretending to
478	      // have. Forgetting it means the next attempt really asks again.
479	      this.#maps.delete(id);
480	      throw failure;
481	    }
482	  }
483	
484	  /**
485	   * One computed world: the map with this branch folded onto it and every
486	   * likelihood worked through time.
487	   *
488	   * @param request Which map, and which branch — sent whole, because there is
489	   *   nowhere to keep one yet.
490	   */
491	  async readWorld(request: WorldRequest): Promise<WorldView> {
492	    const bundle = await this.readBundle(request.baseId);
493	    const branch = request.branch;
494	    const world = await readWorld(
495	      request.baseId,
496	      branch === undefined ? null : sendable(branch),
497	      seedFor(bundle),
498	    );
499	    const view = toWorldView(
500	      world,
501	      {
502	        id: bundle.id,
503	        title: bundle.title,
504	        day: bundle.fixture_date,
505	        origin: originOf(world, bundle, branch?.label ?? null),
506	      },
507	      branch,
508	    );
509	    return branch === undefined ? view : { ...view, branch };
510	  }
511	
512	  /**
513	   * What moved between the map as it was written and the map with this branch
514	   * folded onto it.
515	   *
516	   * @param request Which map and which branch.
517	   */
518	  async readDiff(request: DiffRequest): Promise<DiffView> {
519	    const bundle = await this.readBundle(request.baseId);
520	    const difference = await readDiff(request.baseId, sendable(request.branch), seedFor(bundle));
521	    // The claims are needed only for their words and their kinds, so the rail
522	    // can name an ending rather than print its identifier.
523	    const claims = bundle.graph.propositions.map(toClaim).concat(request.branch.claims);
524	    return toDiffView(difference, claims);
525	  }
526	
527	  /**
528	   * The number on one arrow: its target, with its cause **supposed** true.
529	   *
530	   * @param request Which map, which branch, and which arrow.
531	   */
532	  async readConditional(request: ConditionalRequest): Promise<Known<Ranged>> {
533	    const bundle = await this.readBundle(request.baseId);
534	    const answer = await readConditional(
535	      request.baseId,
536	      request.branch === undefined ? null : sendable(request.branch),
537	      seedFor(bundle),
538	      request.linkId,
539	    );
540	    return filled(answer);
541	  }
542	}

1	/**
2	 * What the canvas draws, written by hand rather than generated.
3	 *
4	 * This is the browser's own view of one world — a map with its numbers filled
5	 * in — and it is deliberately **not** taken from `src/api/schema.ts`. That file
6	 * is generated from the server's description of itself, and the routes that
7	 * serve a computed world are being written at the same time as this canvas. If
8	 * the canvas typed itself against those routes it could not be built until they
9	 * existed, and it would have to be rewritten every time they changed shape.
10	 *
11	 * The rule that shapes everything below: **every slot where a likelihood would
12	 * go is optional.** A number nobody has computed is not a zero and not a blank;
13	 * it is an absence, and an absence carries the reason it is absent — "no
14	 * market", "no engine yet", or a dash inviting the reader's own number. That is
15	 * the whole of the traceability rule as it reaches this layer: nothing on
16	 * screen may be a number nobody can account for.
17	 *
18	 * Nothing in this file, or anywhere under `src/world`, does arithmetic on a
19	 * likelihood. Numbers arrive from the server and are carried, unchanged and at
20	 * full precision, to the moment they are printed.
21	 *
22	 * **One thing here is taken from the generated description after all, and it is
23	 * the exception that proves the rule:** a branch, in the shape the server writes
24	 * one. That shape is not a view of anything — it is what travels back over the
25	 * wire when a world is asked for — so re-stating it by hand would be writing
26	 * down the server's own words and waiting for them to drift.
27	 */
28	
29	import type { components } from "../api/schema";
30	
31	/** What a claim is for. Its shape on the canvas carries this, never its colour. */
32	export type ClaimKind = "hypothesis" | "event" | "market" | "not_tradeable";
33	
34	/**
35	 * How a push behaves when its cause goes away. `trigger` is a toppled domino —
36	 * it stays toppled. `sustain` is an apple on a desk — take the desk away and
37	 * the apple falls.
38	 */
39	export type LinkMode = "trigger" | "sustain";
40	
41	/** Whose number this is. The three are never averaged into one. */
42	export type BeliefOwner = "model" | "user" | "market";
43	
44	/**
45	 * A likelihood and the range around it, both at full precision.
46	 *
47	 * The range says **how sure we are of the number** — not how much the world can
48	 * move. How much the world can move is already inside `p`. Rounding to two
49	 * significant figures happens once, at the moment of display, and never here.
50	 */
51	export interface Ranged {
52	  /** How likely the claim is to come out true, from 0 to 1. */
53	  readonly p: number;
54	  /** The bottom of the range around `p`. Never above it. */
55	  readonly lo: number;
56	  /** The top of the range around `p`. Never below it. */
57	  readonly hi: number;
58	}
59	
60	/**
61	 * Which of the five absences this is. It is what picks the words.
62	 *
63	 * - `no_engine` — nothing has worked this number through the map yet.
64	 * - `no_market` — no venue quotes this claim.
65	 * - `not_said` — nobody has given a number. The one dash on screen with a
66	 *   meaning: the reader's own empty slot, inviting a number.
67	 * - `refused` — the engine was asked and **would not** work this number out. It
68	 *   is its own kind rather than a shade of `no_engine`, because the two are
69	 *   different facts: *nothing has run yet* invites waiting, and *the engine
70	 *   turned this down, here is why* invites repairing the thing it turned down.
71	 *   Reusing one word for both would make the reason on screen the only thing
72	 *   telling them apart, and a reason is not something code can read back.
73	 * - `ask_failed` — the engine was asked and one attempt did not come back. It is
74	 *   the only absence that is not a fact about the map, so it is the only one
75	 *   that is never kept: ask again and it may well be gone.
76	 *
77	 * **The last two are not the same and must not be merged.** A refusal is an
78	 * answer — the engine looked and said no, and said why — and it will say the
79	 * same thing every time until the thing it refused is repaired. A failed ask is
80	 * not an answer at all.
81	 */
82	export type AbsenceKind = "no_engine" | "no_market" | "not_said" | "refused" | "ask_failed";
83	
84	/**
85	 * A number that is not here, and why.
86	 *
87	 * `words` is what the reader sees where the number would have been — "no
88	 * market", "no engine yet", "not worked out", or a dash. `reason` is the sentence
89	 * that says why, so no slot on screen is ever merely empty. `kind` is which of
90	 * the five this is, so that code can tell one absence from another without
91	 * reading its words back — the dash that invites a number is not the dash that
92	 * means nothing was computed, and neither of those is a refusal or an ask that
93	 * did not come back.
94	 */
95	/**
96	 * The mark that says an absence came from the one place absences are made.
97	 *
98	 * **It exists only for the compiler.** It is declared and never defined, so
99	 * nothing is on the object at run time and nothing is carried over a wire — and
100	 * a hand-built `{ kind, words, reason }` does not compile anywhere but
101	 * `world/absence.ts`, which is the one module allowed to promise it. The
102	 * vocabulary says *"these are the words; change them here first"*, and that
103	 * instruction means nothing while a seventh spelling is one object literal away
104	 * — as six files proved by holding one each.
105	 */
106	declare const WRITTEN_HERE: unique symbol;
107	
108	export interface Absence {
109	  /** Which absence this is. */
110	  readonly kind: AbsenceKind;
111	  /** What is printed where the number would be. Never blank, never a zero. */
112	  readonly words: string;
113	  /** Why there is no number, in plain words. */
114	  readonly reason: string;
115	  /** Made by `absence()` or `noReadingAtAll()`, and by nothing else. */
116	  readonly [WRITTEN_HERE]: true;
117	}
118	
119	/**
120	 * A value we may not have, with the reason standing in its place when we do not.
121	 *
122	 * `reading` is optional — every number slot in this view model is — and when it
123	 * is missing, `absence` is present and says why. The two halves are written as
124	 * a choice between two shapes so that the type itself forbids an empty slot
125	 * with no reason attached: there is no way to write one down.
126	 */
127	export type Known<T> =
128	  | { readonly reading: T; readonly absence?: undefined }
129	  | { readonly reading?: undefined; readonly absence: Absence };
130	
131	/** The three voices on one claim, each in its own slot, never merged. */
132	export interface BeliefSlots {
133	  /** What the model thinks. */
134	  readonly model: Known<Ranged>;
135	  /** What the reader thinks. Absent until they say. */
136	  readonly user: Known<Ranged>;
137	  /** What a venue is pricing. Absent when no venue quotes this claim. */
138	  readonly market: Known<Ranged>;
139	}

141	/**

308	/**
309	 * How far a claim's likelihood moved between two worlds, as the engine read it.
310	 *
311	 * Both numbers arrive from the engine at full precision and are printed as they
312	 * came. Which way it went is a word the engine's own reading decides, never a
313	 * subtraction done here — this half of the product does no arithmetic on the
314	 * map's numbers, and "is the second bigger than the first" would be the first
315	 * step down that road.
316	 */
317	export interface Movement {
318	  /** The first world's likelihood, on the claim's own resolve-by day. */
319	  readonly from: number;
320	  /** The second world's likelihood, on the same day. */
321	  readonly to: number;
322	  /** Which way it went. */
323	  readonly way: "up" | "down";
324	  /**
325	   * How far it moved, as the engine reported it.
326	   *
327	   * Carried beside the two readings because a move can be smaller than the
328	   * second significant figure: when the before and the after print the same,
329	   * this is the only thing that says anything moved at all.
330	   */
331	  readonly by: number;
332	  /**
333	   * The share of versions of the map that moved the same way. On screen this is
334	   * headed **same direction**; the word *agreement* is kept off the screen.
335	   */
336	  readonly sameDirection: Known<number>;
337	  /**
338	   * True when the engine says this claim moved **only** because an observation
339	   * made some versions of the map count for more than others.
340	   *
341	   * It comes from the engine's difference, on the claim's own row, and the
342	   * browser must never work it out for itself — whether a claim moved for that
343	   * reason is a fact about how the engine read the numbers, and only the engine
344	   * knows it. The panel prints one sentence when it is set.
345	   */
346	  readonly onlyReweighted?: boolean;
347	}

349	/**
350	 * What an edit did to a claim.
351	 *
352	 * Four of the five are worked out from the branch alone, with no arithmetic
353	 * anywhere: following arrows is walking, not calculating.
354	 *
355	 * - `added` — the claim arrives in an **Add a claim** edit.
356	 * - `killed` — the claim is the target of a **Suppose this is false**. Forced
357	 *   false, full stop. "No path from the hypothesis reaches this any more" is a
358	 *   fact about a route, and the panel's path bar reports it in those words.
359	 * - `downstream` — the claim is in the affected set of at least one edit: a
360	 *   claim your change **can** move. Drawn live, its model number reading its
361	 *   absence, because nothing has worked the new number out.
362	 * - `untouched` — everything else. Identical to the base world, and the map can
363	 *   say so without hedging, because that is a proven property of an edit.
364	 * - `shifted` — the number moved, with a before and an after. It needs two
365	 *   numbers to compare, so only the engine ever produces one, and the browser
366	 *   copies the word across rather than deciding it.
367	 *
368	 * **Which of the two readings wins.** Once the engine has answered, its own word
369	 * is the authority wherever it has one — `added`, `killed` and `shifted` are
370	 * the engine's. `downstream` and `untouched` stay the browser's, because they
371	 * answer a different question: *can* your edit reach this claim, rather than
372	 * *did* its number move. A claim the edit can reach whose number did not move is
373	 * `downstream`, and saying `untouched` about it would be telling the reader
374	 * their change cannot reach something it can.
375	 */
376	export type DiffState = "added" | "killed" | "downstream" | "untouched" | "shifted";

383	 * none of the six operations' code names ever appears in one.

388	  /** What the badge means, for the reader who asks. */

391	   * True when this badge says an earlier one no longer holds, so the tile can

393	   */
394	  readonly overrides?: boolean;
395	  /**
396	   * True when this badge is how far the number moved — `.40 → .30 ▼` — rather

398	   *
399	   * It sits with the badges because it is what the edits did to this claim, and
400	   * because the tile already reserves room for whatever they have to say. It is
401	   * drawn differently: the two readings in the number face with a chevron
402	   * between the old and the new.

404	  readonly movement?: boolean;
405	}

407	/** One arrow, as a wire draws it. */
408	export interface LinkView {
409	  /** The arrow's identifier: its two ends joined, such as `H->B`. */
410	  readonly id: string;
411	  /** The claim the arrow starts at. */
412	  readonly source: string;
413	  /** The claim the arrow ends at. */
414	  readonly target: string;
415	  /** Whether the push survives its cause going away. */
416	  readonly mode: LinkMode;
417	  /**
418	   * How hard this arrow pushes, signed, at full precision.
419	   *
420	   * It is signed **on the claim, not on the world**. The arrow into *Brent
421	   * settles below $68* is `+1.6` — positive, because it makes that claim come
422	   * out true more often — and the thing that claim describes is a *falling*
423	   * price. So a push's sign is not a direction of financial effect, it never
424	   * takes a direction hue, and it is carried by the printed sign and a word.
425	   *
426	   * Nothing on the canvas adds one of these to anything. Choosing a stroke
427	   * width or a word for it is a comparison against fixed thresholds.
428	   */
429	  readonly strength: number;
430	  /** Days from the cause becoming true to the push reaching full size. */
431	  readonly lag: number;
432	  /** What the push does over time. The wire's stroke pattern, and nothing else. */
433	  readonly shape: LinkShape;
434	  /** Days for an `impulse` push to fall to half its size. Absent on the other two shapes. */
435	  readonly halfLife: number | null;
436	  /** The mechanism in one to three plain sentences: why this cause moves this effect. */
437	  readonly rationale: string;
438	  /** What backs the arrow, each with the day it was fetched or the reason there is none. */
439	  readonly sources: readonly SourceView[];
440	  /** Where this arrow came from. Drawn as a mark at the tail, spelled out in the panel. */
441	  readonly provenance: Provenance;
442	  /**
443	   * The target's likelihood with this arrow's source supposed true.
444	   *
445	   * Not computed here and not carried on the world: it costs a whole extra
446	   * run of the map per arrow, so the engine works one out only when a wire is
447	   * asked about. Until then — and always, in this build, because that route
448	   * does not exist yet — the slot holds its absence and the wire's chip reads
449	   * the push back in words instead. Never a guessed number.
450	   */
451	  readonly conditional: Known<Ranged>;
452	  /**
453	   * True when this arrow is a market feeding back on the world. A feedback
454	   * arrow is the one arrow allowed to close a loop, and it is set aside when
455	   * the map is sorted into layers — otherwise there would be no left-to-right
456	   * order to sort it into.
457	   */
458	  readonly reflexive: boolean;
459	  /**
460	   * What an edit did to this arrow. Absent when no edit touched it.
461	   *
462	   * - `added` — an **Add a claim** edit brought it.
463	   * - `cut` — a supposition cut it: "take this as given, and do not tell me what
464	   *   caused it". It is still drawn, faint and dashed, because an arrow that
465	   *   simply vanished would be a change nobody could see.
466	   * - `retuned` — a **Change this push** edit moved its number.
467	   */
468	  readonly change?: "added" | "cut" | "retuned";
469	  /**
470	   * True when this arrow is **not** in the world you are looking at. Drawn faint
471	   * in the same place, so that flipping between the two worlds moves nothing.
472	   *
473	   * A ghost arrow is carried by how faint it is and by nothing else. Its stroke
474	   * is fully spent saying what kind of push it is — dot-dash for a spike that
475	   * fades, solid for a switch that holds, doubled when the push only lasts while
476	   * its cause does — and dashing it to say "other world" as well would leave it
477	   * saying neither clearly.
478	   */
479	  readonly ghost?: boolean;
480	}

663	/**
664	 * One edit in a branch.
665	 *
666	 * The six operations keep their code names — `do`, `observe`, `insert`,
667	 * `retune`, `refine`, `believe` — **in code, in the wire format and in the
668	 * spec, and nowhere on screen.** What the reader sees is the button they
669	 * pressed and the badge it earns, both copied word for word from the shared
670	 * vocabulary. `frontend/src/components/BranchPanel.tsx` is the one place those
671	 * words are written.
672	 */
673	export type Edit =
674	  /** Take this as given, and do not tell me what caused it. */
675	  | {
676	      readonly op: "do";
677	      /** The claim being supposed true or false. */
678	      readonly target: string;
679	      /** True to suppose it holds, false to suppose it does not. */
680	      readonly value: boolean;
681	      /** The day the supposition takes effect, as the map writes a day. */
682	      readonly at: string;
683	    }
684	  /** This is news — update what came before it too. */
685	  | {
686	      readonly op: "observe";
687	      readonly target: string;
688	      readonly value: boolean;
689	      readonly at: string;
690	    }
691	  /** A claim and its arrows arrive together. */
692	  | {
693	      readonly op: "insert";
694	      /** The new claim's identifier on the map. */
695	      readonly claimId: string;
696	      /** The new claim in its own words, which is what the badge quotes. */
697	      readonly words: string;
698	      /** The arrows that attach it. */
699	      readonly arrows: readonly AddedArrow[];
700	      /**
701	       * The whole claim and its arrows, exactly as the engine drafted them.
702	       *
703	       * Present when the part of this product that drafts a claim answered, and
704	       * absent on a branch a stored example shipped with. It is what lets this
705	       * edit be written the server's way and folded back onto the map: a claim is
706	       * not its wording, it is the wording plus how it is judged, by whom, by
707	       * when and what it started from, and a branch carrying only the words
708	       * cannot be folded at all.
709	       */
710	      readonly drafted?: components["schemas"]["Insert"];
711	    }
712	  /** One number on one arrow moves. */
713	  | {
714	      readonly op: "retune";
715	      /** The arrow whose push is being changed. */
716	      readonly link: string;
717	      /** The new push, signed, on the same scale the arrow carries. */
718	      readonly strength: number;
719	      /** What the push was before, so the panel can read the change back. */
720	      readonly wasStrength: number;
721	    }

731	 * A named, ordered list of edits over a base map. A branch *is* the edits.
732	 *
733	 * It holds no likelihoods and no results. `claims` and `links` are the drawable
734	 * detail for what an **Add a claim** edit brought with it, when the map
735	 * supplied a whole claim rather than only its words — the stored example's own
736	 * branch does; a claim the reader types does not, and is shown in the branch
737	 * panel rather than drawn as a tile.
738	 */

740	  /** This branch's identifier. */
741	  readonly id: string;
742	  /** The name the reader reads. */
743	  readonly label: string;
744	  /** Which of the four hues its lane and its name chip take. */
745	  readonly hue: BranchHue;
746	  /** The edits, in the order they were made. Appended to, never rewritten. */
747	  readonly edits: readonly Edit[];
748	  /** Whole claims an edit added, when the map supplied them. */
749	  readonly claims: readonly ClaimView[];
750	  /** Whole arrows an edit added, when the map supplied them. */
751	  readonly links: readonly LinkView[];
752	  /**
753	   * This same branch written the way the server writes one, so it can be sent
754	   * back to be folded onto the map — when it can be.
755	   *
756	   * It is carried rather than rebuilt from `edits` for one reason: an **Add a
757	   * claim** edit brings a whole claim — how it is judged, by whom, by when, what
758	   * it started from — and the drawable form above keeps only what a tile needs.
759	   * Rebuilding the server's form from the drawable one would quietly drop the
760	   * rest, and the map the engine folded would not be the map on screen.
761	   *

763	   * of your own needs the part of this product that drafts one, and that is not
764	   * connected — so a branch holding one cannot be folded, and asking for its
765	   * world says exactly that rather than sending half of it.
766	   *
767	   * Where it is present the two forms are built side by side, from the same

769	   */

774	 * A branch exactly as the server writes one.
775	 *
776	 * Taken from the server's own description of itself, because this shape really
777	 * is the server's: it is what goes back over the wire when a world is asked
778	 * for, and re-stating it here would let the two drift apart.
779	 */
780	export type WireBranch = components["schemas"]["Branch"];

782	/** One edit as the server writes one. */
783	export type WireEdit = components["schemas"]["Branch"]["interventions"][number];

786	 * One ending the edit can reach, as the rail beside the map lists it.
787	 *
788	 * Every number on a row is optional, and before the engine answers every one of
789	 * them is an absence with its reason. **The rail ranks nothing and computes
790	 * nothing**: when the engine has ordered these rows the browser draws them in
791	 * that order, and when it has not the browser says so on its own face.
792	 */

794	  /** The ending's identifier on the map. */
795	  readonly claimId: string;
796	  /** The ending in its own words. */
797	  readonly label: string;
798	  /** What kind of ending it is, which is what says whether anything trades. */
799	  readonly kind: ClaimKind;

807	    readonly by: number;

810	  readonly rangeWidth: Known<number>;
811	  /** Same direction: the share of versions of the map that moved the same way. */

816	   * The engine lists the endings that moved; an ending missing from that list
817	   * could mean either "it did not move" or "it is not on this map", and silence
818	   * cannot be told from absence. So the rail adds a quiet row reading *no
819	   * change* for every ending the edit can reach that the engine left out, after
820	   * the ones it ranked and never mixed in among them.
821	   */
822	  readonly noChange?: boolean;
823	}

826	 * What the panel beside the map is open on, and what the map draws a ring
827	 * around. One name for one thing: the map, the panel and the keyboard all mean
828	 * the same shape by it.
829	 */
830	export type Selection =
831	  | { readonly kind: "claim"; readonly id: string }
832	  | { readonly kind: "wire"; readonly id: string }
833	  /**
834	   * The run that produced the map, rather than anything on it.
835	   *
836	   * The panel's third subject: not a claim and not an arrow, but the generation
837	   * itself — what it cost and every proposal it made, accepted or refused. The
838	   * identifier is the one the engine minted and sent on the run's first event.
839	   * Nothing on the canvas draws a ring for it, because there is nothing on the
840	   * canvas that is it.
841	   */
842	  | { readonly kind: "generation"; readonly id: string }
843	  | null;

1	/**
2	 * Why the engine reports no change on a claim, in one sentence.
3	 *
4	 * **There is one of these sentences in the product and this is it.** The tile's
5	 * movement line, the rail's greyed row and the panel's *what your edit did* all
6	 * read it from here. Before this file there were four of them, written apart,
7	 * and each named a different cause — which is how two of them came to be flatly
8	 * false about half the claims they appeared on.
9	 *
10	 * **What the engine actually says.** A claim comes out `shifted` only when
11	 * *both* halves of its test pass: the move clears a floor, and the versions of
12	 * the map agree on which way it went (`spec/multiverse/diff.md`, and
13	 * `backend/src/katalyst/domain/diff.py` where the two constants live).
14	 * `unchanged` is the default — it is what a claim gets when *either* half fails,
15	 * and the engine does not record which. Neither does its answer: the floor and
16	 * the bar are constants inside the engine and appear nowhere on the wire.
17	 *
18	 * **So this sentence names no cause.** It gives the engine's verdict and the
19	 * engine's own two numbers and stops. Working the cause out here would mean
20	 * hard-coding the engine's floor and its bar in the browser and re-running the
21	 * `shifted` test against them — a second engine on the map, disagreeing with the
22	 * first about which claims held still, with nobody able to say which was right.
23	 * The one exception is the case the engine *does* name, on its own row: a claim
24	 * that moved only because an observation changed how much each version counts.
25	 *
26	 * If the reader should be told which half failed, the engine is the one that can
27	 * say it — either by naming the two constants in its answer or by saying on the
28	 * row which half a claim failed. Until it does, this sentence is the honest one.
29	 */
30	
31	import { toShare, toTwoFigures } from "../../components/BeliefChip";
32	import type { Movement } from "../../world/types";
33	
34	/** What the line reads where a move would go, when the engine says there was none. */
35	export const NO_CHANGE = "no change";
36	
37	/**
38	 * The sentence behind *no change* on one claim.
39	 *
40	 * @param moved What the engine read on this claim: the two numbers, which way
41	 *   they went, and the share of versions that agreed. Absent when the engine
42	 *   reported no pair of readings for it at all — which happens only when one of
43	 *   the two worlds does not hold the claim.
44	 */
45	export function noChangeReason(moved: Movement | undefined): string {
46	  if (moved === undefined) {
47	    return (
48	      "The engine compared the two worlds and reports no change on this claim. It gave no pair " +
49	      "of readings for it, so there is nothing here to put beside the verdict."
50	    );
51	  }
52	  if (moved.onlyReweighted === true) {
53	    // The one cause the engine states outright, on the claim's own row. Inside
54	    // every version of the map the number held exactly still; what moved was how
55	    // much each version counts, which is why no direction was there to agree on.
56	    return (
57	      `The engine reports no change on this claim: inside every version of the map its number ` +
58	      `held still, and what moved was how much each version counts — from ` +
59	      `${toTwoFigures(moved.from)} to ${toTwoFigures(moved.to)} across the lot of them.`
60	    );
61	  }
62	  const agreed = moved.sameDirection.reading;
63	  const versions =
64	    agreed === undefined
65	      ? ""
66	      : `, and ${toShare(agreed)} of the versions of the map moved the same way`;
67	  return (
68	    `The engine compared the two worlds and reports no change on this claim: it read ` +
69	    `${toTwoFigures(moved.from)} then ${toTwoFigures(moved.to)}${versions}. A move is reported ` +
70	    `only when it is far enough and the versions agree on its direction, and this one did not ` +
71	    `clear both. Which of the two it was is the engine's to say, and it does not say.`
72	  );
73	}

1	# The diff view — two worlds in one picture
2	
3	## Purpose
4	
5	You supposed the strait reopens. Then you added a strike the next day. Two maps now exist, and one
6	question matters: **what did my edit reach, and what did it provably leave alone?**
7	
8	The diff view answers it in one picture. Both maps are laid out **once**, together, then painted
9	twice in the same coordinates — the new world solid, the old world faint behind it. Nothing moves
10	between them, so every difference you see is a real difference and not a re-layout.
11	
12	Before the engine exists that answer is **structural** — *here is what your edit can reach, and here
13	is what it cannot* — and where a number will later sit, this stack draws **an absence with its
14	reason**: never a blank, never a zero, never a stand-in.
15	
16	This chapter owns the ghost overlay, the delta rail, the A ⇄ A′ toggle and the branch panel — and,
17	because every number slot on the world uses them, the `Known<T>` and `Absence` shapes the whole of
18	`spec/workbench/` reads.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## Data model
23	
24	### The seam — `WorldSource`
25	
26	The engine (stack 03a) and the canvas (this stack) are built at the same time. One interface keeps
27	them apart, and it is the only place the canvas learns anything:
28	
29	```ts
30	export interface WorldSource {
31	  /** The base map and its branches, as the fixture route already serves them. */
32	  readBundle(id: string): Promise<FixtureBundle>;
33	  /** One world. Its numbers are OPTIONAL — see `Known<T>` below. */
34	  readWorld(request: WorldRequest): Promise<WorldView>;
35	}
36	```
37	
38	Two implementations, and the screen cannot tell which it has. `FixtureWorldSource` reads
39	`GET /api/fixtures/hormuz` and uses the fixture's stored `beliefs.model` for the **base** world —
40	honest, because the fixture says in its own comments that those are illustrative. `ApiWorldSource`
41	calls `POST /api/worlds` and `POST /api/worlds/diff` once they exist.
42	
43	**For the second world, before the engine, there is no second set of numbers at all.** No committed
44	illustrative world, no hand-written likelihoods, no "illustrative numbers" chip. A number nobody
45	computed is exactly the state a reader cannot trace.
46	
47	### `WorldView` — this stack's own view model
48	
49	`WorldView` lives in `frontend/src/world/types.ts` and is **written by hand**, not generated from
50	`frontend/src/api/schema.ts`, which belongs to stack 03a this cycle. Three kinds of absence need
51	three different sentences, so an absence carries both its kind and its sentence:
52	
53	```ts
54	/** A value we may not have. Never a blank, never a zero, never a placeholder.
55	    The two halves are written as a choice between two shapes, so the type itself
56	    forbids an empty slot with no reason attached: there is no way to write one. */
57	export type Known<T> =
58	  | { reading: T; absence?: undefined }
59	  | { reading?: undefined; absence: Absence };
60	
61	export interface Absence {
62	  /** Which absence this is; it picks the words. */
63	  kind: "no_engine" | "no_market" | "not_said";
64	  /** What is printed where the number would be. Never blank, never a zero. */
65	  words: string;
66	  /** The sentence shown beside the words. Always present, never empty. */
67	  reason: string;
68	}
69

162	**`BeliefView`** — one likelihood with its range and a name on it — is defined once in
163	[`tiles-ports-wires.md`](tiles-ports-wires.md), because the belief chip is the only component that

168	model's is `rangeWidth`. Same number, and neither is ever shown — the rail's column is headed **how
169	firm**. Likewise the field `agreement`, whose column reads **same direction**: the bare word
170	*agreement* is left free on screen for a run-to-run number, if one is ever earned. Decision record
171	0015 says not in stack 04 — the range a claim ships with is the one the model stated, labelled as
172	stated, and no number anywhere says how far two generations agreed.
173	
174	**And one field with one spelling in all three places.** The engine's `ClaimDiff` carries
175	`moved_only_by_reweighting`; the view model spells it `movedOnlyByReweighting`; the Inspector turns it
176	into one fixed sentence. Nothing shortens it, nothing abbreviates it, and nothing in the browser
177	decides it — [`inspector.md`](inspector.md) B2 has the sentence and the rule.

201	## Behaviour
202	
203	Worked on the Hormuz map (the cast is in [`README.md`](README.md)). This chapter uses all seven base
204	claims, and the branch `br_hormuz_then_strike`: suppose **H** true on Oct 1; add **S** *a confirmed
205	military strike on Iranian territory* with three arrows (S → B, S → C, S → H); suppose S true on
206	Oct 2. The map's "today" is 2026-10-01.
207	
208	### B1 — One layout, two paintings
209	
210	Lay out the union of both worlds **once**. Every claim in both gets one position. Then paint twice
211	into that one coordinate space: **A′** at full opacity and solid, **A** at **20%** opacity, dashed,
212	behind it. Nothing shifts and nothing fades into anything, so a tile in the same place in both
213	paintings really is the same claim. On Hormuz the union is eight tiles — the seven base claims plus
214	S, the only one with nothing behind it.
215	
216	The hover lens *multiplies* that 20% rather than replacing it
217	([`tiles-ports-wires.md`](tiles-ports-wires.md)), so a tile that is both off the hovered path and
218	old lands near 3% and disappears — which is correct: you asked to see one path in one world.
219	
220	### B2 — The four structural states, computed from the branch
221	
222	Each tile carries a diff state and the state drives how it is drawn. In this stack there are four,
223	and **every one is computed from the branch alone**:
224	
225	| State | Computed from the branch by | Drawn as |
226	|---|---|---|
227	| `added` | The claim arrives in an `insert` | Solid, with an accent ring |
228	| `killed` | The claim is the target of a **Suppose this is false** — full stop | Ghosted, struck through, desaturated |
229	| `downstream` | The claim is in the affected set of at least one edit — a claim your change **can** move | Drawn live, its number slot reading *"no engine yet"* |
230	| `untouched` | Everything else. Byte-identical, and the canvas can say so without hedging | Neutral |
231	
232	**`killed` means forced false and nothing else** (Kent, 2026-09-17). "No path from the hypothesis
233	reaches this claim any more" is a fact about a *route*, not a state of a claim, and the Inspector's
234	path bar reports it in those words. No claim is ever **only in A**, either, because no edit removes
235	one. Nothing in the Hormuz bundle supposes a claim false, so `killed` is drawn but not exercised by
236	the worked example; a unit test over a hand-built branch covers it.
237	
238	**Following arrows is reachability, not arithmetic** — no strength is added, no likelihood is
239	moved, no shape is evaluated. Which claims each operation reaches, and which arrows count, are both
240	settled in [`../multiverse/interventions.md`](../multiverse/interventions.md): the affected-set
241	table, and one named rule — *the map the engine works through is the map with feedback arrows set
242	aside*. Anything asking **what can move** reads that map, these diff states included; anything
243	asking **what can I walk to** reads the whole map — the hover lens, `h`/`l`, the outline.
244	
245	On the strike branch: **S** is `added`; **H** is `downstream`, because S → H was inserted *after*
246	the supposition on H and so is live; **C** and **B** are `downstream` from H and again directly from
247	S; **N1** through H → N1; **M1** and **M2** from B. And, as a consequence of that rule:
248	
249	> **R — *OPEC+ announces output restraint* — is `untouched`. Nothing on this branch can reach it.**
250	
251	R's only incoming arrow is B → R, the **feedback** arrow — a price outcome acting back on what
252	producers do. Set aside, R has no incoming arrow at all: an ancestor of B, never a descendant of
253	anything this branch touches. So the screen can say out loud: *your strike moves the oil price, the
254	insurance premium, both contracts and the diplomatic ending — and it cannot move OPEC's
255	announcement.* That sentence is the product, and `INV-workbench.41` and `.42` below pin it.
256	
257	### B3 — The fifth state arrives with the engine, and nothing is deleted
258	
259	`shifted` — a before and an after with a directional chevron — needs two numbers to compare, so it
260	cannot exist here. When `ApiWorldSource` is switched on in stack 04 the empty slots fill and `shifted`
261	appears. **Nothing written in this stack is deleted then, because nothing false was written.** The
262	authority changes hands: the server's `affected_set` becomes the truth and the browser's structural
263	states become a **hint that must agree with it**, pinned by a component test on the Hormuz branch. A
264	browser quietly disagreeing with the engine about what an edit reached is the traceability veto
265	wearing a disguise.
266	
267	### B4 — A ⇄ A′ is a hard switch, never a crossfade
268	
269	`Space` swaps which world is solid — an instant switch, not a fade. Two half-drawn worlds on top of
270	each other is a picture of nothing, and a crossfade invites the eye to read the blur as a number
271	moving. The transition is **scrubbable**: sit on either side, go back and forth, and the map never
272	re-lays-out. Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` there is nothing to remove, because there was
273	never a tween.
274	
275	### B5 — The delta rail, before the engine and after
276	
277	The rail sits beside the canvas and lists what changed at the **endings** — the claims that name an
278	instrument, or name why there is none. **With the engine** it is the terminal changes, ranked, one
279	line each, in the order the engine gave them:
280	
281	```
282	M1  A Polymarket contract "Brent below $70 on 2026-10-31" resolves YES.
283	    tradeable
284	    down · largest on 2026-10-04
285	    .49 ▼ .42        .27        95%
286	```
287	
288	The ending's own words and what kind of ending it is; then which way it went and
289	the day the two worlds are furthest apart; then the three columns — the change,
290	**how firm**, **same direction**. The chevron sits between the two readings
291	rather than after them, so the row reads as one number becoming another, and the
292	direction is a word as well as a glyph because a glyph read aloud is nothing at
293	all.
294	
295	The engine writes every part of that row. On the Hormuz strike branch (seed 20261001) it gives
296	**two** rows: the Polymarket Brent contract · `.49 → .42` ▼ · largest on Oct 4; and the energy-shares
297	claim · `.43 → .36` ▼ · largest on Oct 6. This stack draws neither number; it asks for neither.
298	
299	**The third ending is the one worth reading.** N1, the talks that cannot be traded, makes the biggest
300	move on the map — `.28 → .38` — and the engine still calls it `unchanged`, so it is **not** a ranked
301	row. Its only incoming arrow is the map's one bare assertion, `H → N1`, and a bare assertion is drawn
302	so wide that only 88 of every 100 versions of the map agree the talks go *up* at all — under the 90
303	in 100 the engine needs before it will say a claim moved
304	([`../multiverse/diff.md`](../multiverse/diff.md) owns that bar). A big move nobody can agree the
305	direction of is exactly what the bar is for, and the rail still lists N1: greyed, beneath the two
306	ranked rows, reading **no change**. That is the case B5's greyed row was written for, arriving.
307	
308	That order is the size of the move times the **weakest arrow on the best-backed route** from any of
309	the branch's edits to that ending — the route whose weakest arrow is strongest. Two factors and no
310	more; the engine computes it, the rail renders it in the order given, and beside it sit **two
311	columns that are never folded into the rank**:
312	
313	| Column on screen | The question it answers | Field |
314	|---|---|---|
315	| **how firm** | *How firm is this number?* The width of the new world's own range on that claim — the same quantity the tile shows, so the rail and the tile cannot disagree | `rangeWidth` |
316	| **same direction** | *Did it point the same way whatever numbers we started from?* The share of the 2 000 versions of the map that moved in the same direction — **each version counted by as much as it counted for the two numbers**, so a version that contributed nothing to either number votes on neither | `agreement` |
317	
318	Different questions, weighed separately by a trader, which is why they are columns and not one
319	score. Folding width into the rank would sink exactly the claims that most deserve attention.
320	
321	**An ending that did not move is a greyed row reading *no change*, never a missing one** *(decided
322	2026-09-17, stack 04a; this closes [`../multiverse/diff.md`](../multiverse/diff.md) open question
323	5)*. The engine's `rows` hold only the endings that came out `shifted`, so a reader looking at that
324	list alone cannot tell *"it did not move"* from *"it is not on this map"* — and silence that could
325	mean either is the state the traceability rule exists to forbid. So the rail draws **every ending the
326	edit can reach**: the engine's rows first, in the engine's order, and beneath them, greyed and
327	unranked, in map order, every other reachable ending, each reading **no change** where the move would
328	be.
329	
330	Where that verdict comes from matters as much as the row. The engine's `Diff` carries a `claims` map
331	with **every** claim in either world exactly once and its state, so *did not move* is a fact the
332	engine already states, read off `ClaimDiff.state`. The browser never decides it by comparing two
333	numbers — that would be the browser re-running the shifted test, with its own .005 floor and its own
334	90% bar, and two answers to that question is one too many. The two numbers behind a greyed row are
335	still one click away in the Inspector; the row itself says the thing that is true, which is that
336	nothing here moved.
337	
338	**And the row now says which half of the test it failed.** *Barely moved* and *moved, but the
339	versions disagreed which way* are two different findings, and a reader given only "no change" cannot
340	tell them apart. The engine writes the word — `under_the_floor` or `versions_disagree` — on the
341	claim's own row, and the browser picks the sentence that goes with it. It still works nothing out:
342	the floor and the bar are constants inside the engine and are on no wire, so the browser could not
343	re-run the test if it wanted to. On the Hormuz strike branch the two claims that moved and still came
344	out `unchanged`, B and N1, read `versions_disagree`; R, which did not move at all, reads
345	`under_the_floor`. Where a claim fails both halves the engine names the floor, because a move nobody
346	would notice needs no second sentence about its direction —
347	[`../multiverse/diff.md`](../multiverse/diff.md) owns that rule and the two constants.
348	
349	**Before the engine — this stack — the rail does not rank and does not compute.** It lists the
350	terminals the edit can reach, in **map order**, each with an absence and a reason where the number
351	will go:
352	
353	```
354	                                                   change          how firm   same direction
355	M1  Polymarket "Brent below $70 on 2026-10-31"     no engine yet   —          —
356	M2  XLE underperforms SPY by more than 3%          no engine yet   —          —
357	N1  Omani-mediated talks resume                    no engine yet   —          —
358	```
359	
360	Each dash carries the same reason as the change beside it: no engine yet. All three endings are
361	reachable here, so all three are listed; R is not a terminal and never appears. **A rail that
362	invented an ordering would be inventing the one thing the rail exists to tell you** — map order is
363	visibly arbitrary and says so; a fabricated ranking looks like an answer.
364	
365	**The one-line summary** (FR-16) has a fixed second form for the case where the rail
366	has nothing to report: *"<edit> moves no ending and leaves <n> claims untouched."* Both forms are
367	sentences the world carries. Before the engine the summary is an absence with its reason, like every
368	other computed thing on this screen.
369	
370	**What the rail is read in, top to bottom: the heading, the rows, the note about the order, the
371	summary, the reason line.** The rows come straight after the heading because *what did my edit do,
372	ranked* is what the rail exists to answer, and it used to sit under seven lines of prose — a
373	four-or-five-line summary and a three-line note, at the panel's width. The note about the order
374	reads as a caption to the table and is one; the summary is a sentence about the whole edit and
375	closes. Nothing about what the rail may honestly *say* moved with it: ranked against unranked, the
376	*no change* row and the reason line are exactly as they were.
377	
378	### B6 — UX-14: an assertion a later edit overrode says so
379	
380	A claim the user supposed true, and that a later edit in the same branch pushed back down, is
381	**never drawn as plainly true**. H's tile carries both states in order, word for word:
382	
383	> **Supposed · Oct 1 → Retracted · Oct 2 · by "a confirmed military strike on Iranian territory"**
384	
385	**While an edit has fixed a claim's value, its tile shows the word where a likelihood would go** —
386	*Supposed · Oct 1* where the user took it as given, *Happened · Oct 1* where they reported it as
387	news, *Did not happen · Oct 1* where the news is that it did not (Kent, 2026-09-21, G12) — not
388	`1.0`, not `.98` and not `>.99`. Either way the claim is settled in every simulated world
389	while it holds, so there is no number to show, and inventing one answers a question nobody asked.
390	**This is one rule, not a rule about suppositions**: it reaches the chip, the movement row, the rail
391	row and the panel alike, and nothing but the path product reads the stored number underneath.
392	
393	After the retraction the claim passes through three named states. **Every part of the line and the
394	series is data, never inference** — and this stack has some of it and not the rest:
395	
396	| Part | On Hormuz | Comes from | Needs the world? |
397	|---|---|---|---|
398	| **Supposed · Oct 1** | Oct 1; H shows the word, not a number | The assignment itself: an earlier supposition on H, with its date | **No** — the branch carries it |
399	| **Retracted · Oct 2 · by "…"** | Oct 2 | **The world's own `retractions`**, once there is a world; derived from the branch until then | **Yes, once there is one** — see below |
400	| **withdrawn** | Oct 2 – Oct 4, `.36`, labelled *"withdrawn — no live push yet"* | The `states` series: the cause of the opposing arrow became true on the 2nd, so we stop taking the user's word; S → H's three-day delay has not run, so H reads its own prior again | **Yes** |
401	| **pushed** | Oct 5 onward, `.086` | The `states` series: the delay has run and S → H's −1.9 push lands on that prior | **Yes** |
402	
403	So in this stack H's tile carries the badge pair and its order, its number slot reads *"no engine
404	yet"*, and the series is absent with its reason. (`.086` and not `.09`: two significant figures on
405	every number, the rule [`keyboard-and-access.md`](keyboard-and-access.md)
406	owns. And `.36` rather than H's stated prior of `.35` — reading a prior back through the engine
407	lands a hair above the middle for a likelihood under a half, which decision record 0014 predicts and
408	the golden series confirms.)
409	
410	**The three-day gap between the badge's date and the day the number moves is honest, not something
411	to smooth away.** A supposition ends the day its undermining *cause* becomes true, not the day that
412	arrow's push arrives — otherwise "do I still take your word for this" would hang on a delay
413	parameter, and changing a lag from three days to thirty would let the supposition outlive the news
414	(decision record 0014).
415	
416	**The badge comes from the world** *(decided 2026-09-17, stack 04a; this closes open question 1
417	below)*. A world carries `retractions`, one `Retraction` per supposition that actually ended, and
418	each one names the claim, **the day the cause became true** (never that day plus the arrow's delay),
419	the arrow that undermined it, that arrow's source — which is the claim the badge quotes — and which
420	edit introduced the arrow ([`../multiverse/propagation.md`](../multiverse/propagation.md)). The
421	moment `ApiWorldSource` is switched on, the tile reads that record and **the derivation from the
422	branch stops, rather than staying on as a fallback.** Two derivations of one line eventually
423	disagree, and a badge that says two different things on two screens is the traceability veto wearing
424	a badge; one of them had to become the only one, and the world's is the one with the day the engine
425	actually used.
426	
427	Three consequences worth stating. The branch derivation is **deleted, not kept behind a condition**
428	— a fallback nobody exercises is a second answer waiting to be wrong, and a world that failed to
429	arrive already falls back to the fixture and says so. When the world carries no retraction for a
430	claim, **the tile carries no badge**: silence from the engine is an answer, not a gap to fill in.
431	And the engine can name the edit responsible for every retraction as a matter of theorem rather than
432	of convention — supposing a claim cuts every arrow pointing at it at that moment, so any arrow that
433	later pushes against it was added afterwards, by an edit — so the badge's *by "…"* is never empty.
434	
435	### B7 — The branch panel: a sequence, not a surprise
436	
437	The panel lists that branch's edits **in the order they were made**, each with the badge its
438	operation earns. Read as a sequence, the rule that a later addition outranks an earlier supposition
439	is obvious; met as a number that moved on its own, it reads as a bug.
440	
441	```
442	Hormuz opens, then Iran is struck                        ● violet
443	 1  The Strait of Hormuz reopens…                        Supposed · Oct 1
444	 2  A confirmed military strike on Iranian territory.    Added
445	 3  A confirmed military strike on Iranian territory.    Supposed · Oct 2
446	```
447	
448	**The six buttons and their badges**, copied word for word from
449	[`../vocabulary.md`](../vocabulary.md)'s *Interface words* table — copy, never paraphrase:
450	
451	| Code name (never on screen) | The button | The badge afterwards |
452	|---|---|---|
453	| `do` | **Suppose this is true** (and **Suppose this is false**) | **Supposed · date** |
454	| `observe` | **This happened** | **Happened · date**, and **Did not happen · date** where the news is that it did not |
455	| `insert` | **Add a claim**, hinted as "…but this also happens" | **Added** |
456	| `retune` | **Change this push** | **Retuned** |
457	| `refine` | **Split this claim** | **Split** |
458	| `believe` | **My own number** | none — the three-up belief chip is the badge |
459	
460	And one derived badge no button produces: **Retracted · date · by "…"**. The six code names live in
461	the code, the wire format and the spec, and **none of them ever appears on screen**.
462	
463	Three rules in this stack:
464	
465	1. **The buttons build a branch and show it. They do not move a number.** **My own number** and
466	   **Change this push** append an edit and the panel shows it immediately; the likelihood slots stay
467	   as they were, reading their absence.
468	2. **Split this claim** is **not offered at all** until it is built (stack 06). It was a row that took a press and then said it could do nothing, which was honest and was still a seventh of this menu spent on something a reader cannot take up. Never silently inert, and now never inert: every control on the panel does something when it is pressed. Its words stay settled in [`../vocabulary.md`](../vocabulary.md) for the day the operation arrives.
469	3. **Edits are appended, never edited in place.** The branch is the audit trail, and an audit trail
470	   you can edit is not one.

474	## INVARIANTS
475	
476	Each is *for all X, statement P holds*, and each names what checks it: a component test, or a
477	numbered line of the **visual review checklist** in [`README.md`](README.md). Frontend test names
478	are `test_snake_case`. Short file names below: **diffState** is
479	`frontend/src/graph/__tests__/diffState.test.ts`, **deltaRail**
480	`frontend/src/components/__tests__/deltaRail.test.tsx`, **ghostOverlay**
481	`frontend/src/components/__tests__/ghostOverlay.test.tsx`. This chapter uses `INV-workbench.40` …
482	`.49`.
483	
484	**INV-workbench.40 — one layout, two paintings.** For every claim present in both worlds, its
485	position in the A painting equals its position in the A′ painting, and toggling A ⇄ A′ changes no
486	position anywhere. That the union layout is itself stable is
487	[`layout-and-zoom.md`](layout-and-zoom.md)'s. *Tests:* ghostOverlay ›
488	`test_paints_both_worlds_from_one_position_map`, `test_space_changes_no_position`.
489	
490	**INV-workbench.41 — every diff state is derived, never assigned.** For every claim in a branch
491	world, its `DiffState` is a function of the base map and the branch's edits alone: no component sets
492	a state and no state is read from a number. *Test:* diffState ›
493	`test_computes_the_four_structural_states_for_the_strike_branch`.
494	
495	**INV-workbench.42 — what an edit cannot reach is said so.** For every claim outside the affected
496	set of every edit in the branch, the state is `untouched`. On the Hormuz strike branch that set is
497	exactly `{R}`. *Tests:* diffState › `test_r_comes_out_untouched`; `frontend/e2e/hormuz.spec.ts` ›
498	`test_the_fully_separated_claim_does_not_change`.
499	
500	**INV-workbench.43 — the browser never out-votes the engine.** For the Hormuz branch, every state
501	the browser computed equals the state derived from the server's `affected_set`. Both read the map
502	with feedback arrows set aside, which is why they can agree at all; the day stack 06 unrolls them,
503	`test_a_feedback_arrow_never_carries_a_change` in the domain fails loudly and points at the one
504	sentence to change. Until stack 03a lands this test is skipped with its reason written in it, never
505	deleted. *Test:* diffState › `test_the_browser_states_agree_with_the_engine`.
506	
507	**INV-workbench.44 — `shifted` is never produced without two numbers.** For every pair of worlds in
508	which either side's likelihood is absent, no claim is `shifted`. *Test:* diffState ›
509	`test_never_shifts_on_an_absent_number`.
510	
511	**INV-workbench.45 — no number slot is ever blank.** For every claim and every delta row in this
512	view, a slot without a value renders its `Absence.reason` as words — no empty string, no zero, no
513	dash-without-meaning (the one dash with a meaning is the empty user belief, absence kind
514	`not_said`). *Test:* deltaRail › `test_renders_a_reason_for_every_absent_number`; **visual review
515	checklist line 5**.
516	
517	**INV-workbench.46 — the rail invents no order, and silence is never absence.** Two statements, one
518	subject: the rail neither ranks what nothing has ranked nor leaves out what nothing said was
519	missing. While `ranked` is false the rail renders the reachable terminals in the order the base map
520	stores them, independent of every number on the world. Once the engine ranks them, every reachable
521	terminal is still on the rail — one the engine reported as `shifted` in the order the engine gave,
522	and one it did not as a greyed row reading *no change*, in map order beneath them — and the
523	`shifted` flag on every row is read off the engine's `ClaimDiff`, never derived by comparing two
524	numbers in the browser. A greyed row's sentence is picked by the engine's own word for which half of
525	the test failed, and by no other route: no floor and no bar is written down in the browser. *Tests:*
526	deltaRail › `test_lists_reachable_terminals_in_map_order`, `test_the_rail_keeps_the_engines_order`,
527	`test_an_unmoved_terminal_is_a_greyed_row_not_a_missing_one`,
528	`test_the_no_change_sentence_comes_from_the_engines_own_word`.
529	
530	**INV-workbench.47 — how firm and same direction are never folded into the rank.** For every rail
531	row the two are rendered as their own columns, and no ordering function reads either. *Test:*
532	deltaRail › `test_how_firm_and_same_direction_are_columns_not_factors`.
533	
534	**INV-workbench.48 — a claim whose value an edit fixed shows the word, and the retraction comes from
535	the world.** For every claim under a live supposition and every claim reported as news, the tile
536	renders **Supposed · date**, **Happened · date** or — where the news is that it did not happen —
537	**Did not happen · date** where a likelihood would go, and renders no
538	likelihood for it at all; where a later edit undermined the supposition, both
539	states render in order with the arrow between them. And for every world that carries `retractions`,
540	every **Retracted · date · by "…"** badge on screen is read from that record — its day, its arrow and
541	its quoted claim — with no code path deriving one from the branch; a claim the world reports no
542	retraction for carries no such badge. *Tests:*
543	`frontend/src/components/__tests__/beliefChip.test.tsx` ›
544	`test_a_supposed_claim_renders_the_word_not_a_number`;
545	`frontend/src/components/__tests__/tile.test.tsx` › `test_the_retraction_badge_comes_from_the_world`;
546	**visual review checklist line 12**.
547	
548	**INV-workbench.49 — the branch is append-only and reads in vocabulary words.** For every sequence
549	of button presses, the branch is the edits in the order they were made with no earlier edit altered,
550	and every badge on screen is one of the six — the five in the *Interface words* table plus the
551	derived **Retracted · date · by "…"** — with no code name anywhere. *Tests:*
552	`frontend/src/world/__tests__/branchReducer.test.ts` ›
553	`test_appends_edits_in_order_and_never_rewrites_one`, `test_renders_only_interface_words`; **visual
554	review checklist line 11**.
555	
556	---
557	
558	## ANTI-PATTERNS
559	
560	1. **Do not commit a second set of numbers to make the diff look finished.** *Because* a number
561	   nobody computed cannot be traced to an input, a rule or a source — a veto condition — and once an
562	   illustrative world is in the tree everything downstream quietly believes it. **Instead:** ship the
563	   structure, which is real, and let every number slot render its absence with a reason.
564	
565	2. **Do not crossfade A into A′** — stated as an anti-pattern in
566	   [`color-motion-type.md`](color-motion-type.md), which owns motion. Here it means a hard switch on
567	   `Space`, scrubbable, both worlds always in the same coordinates.
568	
569	3. **Do not lay out A and A′ separately and place them side by side.** *Because* two layouts mean
570	   every tile moves a little, and a reader cannot tell a real change from a layout change.
571	   **Instead:** lay out the union once and paint into it twice.
572	
573	4. **Do not rank the delta rail before something has ranked it.** *Because* a ranking is a claim
574	   about which change matters most, and an invented one is a lie in the exact place the reader came
575	   for the truth. **Instead:** map order, visibly arbitrary, until the engine supplies its own.
576	
577	5. **Do not render a claim whose value an edit fixed as `1.0`, `.98`, `>.99` or a full bar** —
578	   supposed or reported as news alike. *Because* a number invites the reader to wonder about the
579	   missing two per cent, and there is no such uncertainty. **Instead:** the word, and its date.
580	
581	6. **Do not let a button move a number in this stack, and do not rewrite an edit in place.**
582	   *Because* a canvas that computes its own likelihoods is a second engine, and two engines
583	   disagree; and because an edited history explains nothing. **Instead:** append an edit and let the
584	   number wait for the engine, saying so meanwhile.
585	
586	---
587	
588	## Open questions
589	
590	*Raised 2026-09-17. Four questions this chapter opened were settled by Kent the same day and now
591	read as statements in the body: which arrows carry a change (B2), what `killed` means (B2), which
592	columns the rail shows (B5), and what the one-line summary says when nothing moved (B5).*
593	
594	**Nothing is open in this chapter.** Two more were settled in stack 04a and now read as statements
595	in the body:
596	
597	1. **Does the retraction badge need the world, or is the branch enough for good?**
598	   **Decided 2026-09-17 (stack 04a): it comes from the world.** `World.retractions` carries the day,
599	   the arrow, the claim to quote and the edit responsible, and the branch derivation is deleted
600	   rather than kept as a fallback — two derivations of one line eventually disagree. In B6, and
601	   pinned by INV-workbench.48.
602	2. **Should the rail ever show an ending that did not move?** Raised on the engine's side, as
603	   [`../multiverse/diff.md`](../multiverse/diff.md) open question 5, and left there for this part to
604	   answer. **Decided 2026-09-17 (stack 04a): yes — a greyed row reading *no change*,** because a
605	   reader cannot tell "it did not move" from "it is not on this map" by looking at a list something
606	   was left out of. In B5, and pinned by INV-workbench.46. Nothing changes on the engine's side: the
607	   verdict is already on `ClaimDiff.state`.
